# Nonvertex gains: parity deficits and a limitation of deletion

This note records a quantitative consequence of nonvertex-fiber-strict-ordinary-depth-improvement.md. It is valid beyond the class with at most \(2^n\) positive fibers, but does not reduce every source to that class.

Let \(d\ge1\), let \(P\) be the finite positive full-\(d\)-volume base set, let \(T=\sum_{z\in P}|K_z|\), and write \(B_{\max}\) for the maximum absolute mixed depth. Set \(N=2^n\), and let \(\mathcal A\) be the occupied parity classes, of cardinality \(J\le N\). Define \(m_c\) and the residual \(R\) as in parity-maxima-residual-and-volume-monotone-forest.md.

## 1. Explicit certificates at the parity maxima

For each \(c\in\mathcal A\), choose a mass-maximizing base \(v_c\). If it is nonvertex, choose an anchored Carathéodory representation and use the explicit gain \(G_c>0\) from the strict-gain theorem. If it is a vertex, put \(G_c=0\). Then
\[
              B_{\max}\ge \Gamma_d m_c+G_c
                    \qquad(c\in\mathcal A).              \tag{1}
\]
The stronger own-body quantity \(A(K_{v_c})+G_c\) may replace the right side. Ties in a class can be resolved to use the largest of any finitely chosen certified gains; nothing depends on selecting a particular maximizing base in advance.

Summing (1) over the occupied classes gives
\[
 \boxed{\quad
       B_{\max}\ge
       \frac{\Gamma_d(T-R)+\sum_{c\in\mathcal A}G_c}{J}.
       \quad}                                           \tag{2}
\]
For example, the concrete sufficient condition
\[
       \sum_cG_c\ge
          \Gamma_d\left[R-\left(1-\frac JN\right)T\right] \tag{3}
\]
implies the OC target \(\Gamma_dT/N\). A negative right side is already covered by the ordinary parity-maximal fiber bound.

Conversely, any source satisfying \(B_{\max}\le\Gamma_dT/N\) must obey
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 R\ge\left(1-\frac JN\right)T+\frac1{\Gamma_d}\sum_cG_c.
 \quad}                                                  \tag{4}
\]
The inequality is strict for an actual strict failure \(B_{\max}<\Gamma_dT/N\). More precisely each selected nonvertex parity maximum satisfies
\[
                  m_c\le\frac TN-\frac{G_c}{\Gamma_d},    \tag{5}
\]
again strictly in a strict failure. This is a shape-sensitive strengthening of the simple bound \(m_c\le T/N\).

These formulas only charge one constructed point per class through its absolute depth; no cap contributions from different candidate points are summed into a single halfspace.

## 2. Uniform noncollapse version

Suppose every fiber needed in the chosen anchored representations, including their target fibers, has volume at least \(\nu>0\) and fits in a ball of radius \(R_0\), with the ball centers unrestricted. Each representation can use at most \(n+1\) other bases. The explicit constants of the strict-gain theorem therefore give one number
\[
                         G_0=G_0(d,n,R_0,\nu)>0
\]
valid at every selected nonvertex maximum, with no lower bound on its anchored coefficients and no bound on the integer base coordinates.

If \(J_{\rm nv}\) selected parity maxima are nonvertices, (4) yields
\[
             R\ge\left(1-\frac JN\right)T
                             +\frac{J_{\rm nv}G_0}{\Gamma_d}. \tag{6}
\]
This is a genuine quantitative exclusion under stated noncollapse bounds. It does not assert that \(G_0/T\) remains positive when those bounds degenerate or the total source mass grows.

## 3. Uniform strict gain still does not make normalized deletion monotone

The exact family from candidate a57c113e8e14cc38 has \(n=d=1\),
\[
 K_{-1}=K_1=[0,1],\qquad K_0=[0,b],\qquad 1\le b\le5.
                                                               \tag{7}
\]
These are the actual fibers of the nested convex pentagons
\[
 \{(z,x):-1\le z\le1,\quad 0\le x\le b-(b-1)|z|\},
\]
with the rectangle interpretation at \(b=1\). Changing \(b\) is precisely the exact one-nonvertex-fiber deletion interpolation.

The middle ordinary absolute maximum is \(b/2\). Its actual mixed maximum, also the global absolute maximum, is
\[
 A(b)=
 \begin{cases}
  (b+5)/4,&1\le b\le3,\\
  (b+1)/2,&3\le b\le5.
 \end{cases}
\]
Thus throughout this whole noncollapsing family,
\[
                        A(b)-b/2\ge1/2.                 \tag{8}
\]
Nevertheless, dividing by the actual total mass \(b+2\),
\[
 \beta(b)=
 \begin{cases}
  (b+5)/(4(b+2)),&1\le b\le3,\\
  (b+1)/(2(b+2)),&3\le b\le5,
 \end{cases}
\]
is strictly decreasing before \(b=3\) and strictly increasing after it. Its minimum \(2/5\) is attained at the interior parameter \(b=3\), while \(\beta(1)=1/2\) and \(\beta(5)=3/7\).

Consequently a uniform strict local gain at a nonvertex does not itself permit a monotone reduction of the normalized optimization problem by deleting that fiber. No collapse is involved: all volumes stay between one and five and all intervals fit in radius-\(5/2\) balls.

This example is above the actual \(n=d=1\) OC target \(1/4\). It obstructs the proposed deletion inference, not a possible deeper classification of sharp global sources. Formulas (2)--(6) are the valid quantitative conclusions currently obtained from the strict gain.
